page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton family, specifically featuring ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core (8 vCPUs total), 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 474 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark measurements reveal strong memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 3,116.41, placing it in the top 10% of evaluated hardware. General computational throughput remains firmly in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,754.0 and multi-core score of 9,950.0, alongside stress-ng results reaching 13,645.04 multi-core. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top 25% at 14.08 GB/sec. Conversely, cryptographic PassMark operations register in the lower 25% (1,507.33), and medium-sized LLM prompt processing (7B model) falls into the bottom 10% at 15.42 tokens per second.

The integration of dedicated physical ARMv9 cores coupled with high-speed local NVMe storage delivers strong resource predictability and I/O efficiency without hyperthreading contention. Because of its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation and attached NVMe SSD disk, the m8gd.2xlarge is technically aligned with transactional databases, caching layers like Redis, CI/CD compilation workloads, and low-latency web serving.
